title: The First Detection of a Pulsar with ALMA
question: At what wavelengths does pulsar emission transition from coherent to incoherent; what is the Vela pulsar's mm/sub-mm spectrum?

what.value: Pulsar radio position and proper motion

evidence.quote: using its radio coordinates as a reference (Dodson et al. 2003)
eight flux density values in the frequency range between 400 MHz and 24 GHz (Manchester et al. 2005; Johnston et al. 2006; Keith et al. 2011)

external_data.citation: Manchester et al. 2005; Johnston et al. 2006; Keith et al. 2011

what.value: UV-optical-NIR PL spectrum and Ks flux

evidence.quote: flat UV-optical-near-IR PL spectrum (Zyuzin et al. 2013)
extrapolation of the mid-IR flux densities (Danilenko et al. 2011)

recipe.method: CASA 4.5.3 + ALMA pipeline calibration; natural-weighted clean images per band
Compute pulsar position at observing epochs from radio coordinates and proper motion; compare with ALMA source position
Fit elliptical Gaussian within 1 arcsec square aperture centred on the pulsar

recipe.goal: Fit mm spectrum and derive brightness temperature
recipe.method: Power-law fit to four flux densities; compare with radio and IR/optical extrapolations; Tb from radio-peak flux for emitting region smaller than a neutron star radius
assumptions: emitting region of one neutron star radius (or 50 R_NS alternative)

recipe.method: Flux down to 5 sigma contour in Band 7; compare with HST, Chandra, Gemini and archival VLT/NACO Ks images

evidence.quote: which corresponds to a PL with $\alpha = -0.79 \pm 0.02$
the Band 7 luminosity of the nebula would be $\sim 6 \times 10^{25}$ erg s$^{-1}$

not_stated_but_needed: clean threshold, niter, cell and image size
whether pipeline products or re-calibrated data were used
how the 10% flux error was combined with statistical error
brightness temperature emitting-size assumptions in detail
score_reason: Simple recipe and public data, but imaging parameters are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, point-source flux measurements and a power-law fit with numeric answers.
